brief: UBS's Chief Investment Office argues Meta Muse's early traction (about 1.8 million iOS downloads in the US and Canada in its first 12 days versus about 1.3 million for ChatGPT over a comparable period, plus higher daily active users and the top US app store rank) is evidence that consumer AI agents may be nearing mainstream adoption. Muse is not the first agent (GrokBot, Instinct exist), but Meta's compute, capital and distribution give it scale advantages. UBS expects this to trigger an agent arms race among Google, Amazon and OpenAI, and to create platform conflict over data and transaction control: Amazon has blocked Muse from its marketplace over unauthorized-activity and transparency concerns, while Shopify has partnered with Muse for agent checkout. Because agents execute tasks rather than just answer questions, UBS sees a new transaction-economics monetization layer forming alongside Meta's existing free/$20/$100 subscription tiers, addressable against a $6tr+ global e-commerce market. UBS says the most attractive investor exposure is the CPU supply chain (AMD, Intel, Arm, TSMC, ASE Technology, SK Hynix, and indirectly AMAT/ASML/Lam Research), since agentic workloads are more CPU-intensive than chatbots. UBS also stays constructive on hyperscalers, though it expects application-layer leadership to keep rotating.
